description: I'm a farmer in Andhra Pradesh, I own 2 acres, and my daughter is in 11th class.
notes: Landholding farmer family qualifies for both the central income support and Andhra Pradesh's YSR Rythu Bharosa top-up (₹13,500/yr, any landholding size). Daughter's education needs more detail (class 11 is post-matric) before matching a scholarship.

description: I am a farmer in Bihar, I own half an acre, and I want to insure my crop.
notes: Small landholding still qualifies for income support and crop insurance (cultivator with land ownership proof).

description: I own 10 acres of farmland in Punjab and I file income tax returns every year.
notes: PM-KISAN explicitly excludes farmer families where a member paid income tax in the last assessment year — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I live abroad now but my family still owns farmland in Maharashtra. Can I get the farmer income support?
notes: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (Maharashtra's PM-KISAN top-up) explicitly excludes NRIs — a deliberate exclusion test grounded in the actual scheme text.

description: I don't own any land, but I lease one acre from a landowner in Andhra Pradesh to grow vegetables. I belong to the ST community.
notes: YSR Rythu Bharosa explicitly covers landless tenant cultivators with a lease agreement (minimum 0.5 acre for vegetable crops), and gives preference to ST tenants. PM-KISAN needs land ownership, so it doesn't apply here.

description: My husband, a registered farmer in Maharashtra, died in a farm accident. He was 42.
notes: Covers accidental death of a registered Maharashtra farmer aged 10-75; excludes natural death, suicide, and pre-existing conditions, so the cause of death should be confirmed as accidental before finalizing.

description: I am a farmer in Telangana, 45 years old, and I want life insurance in case something happens to me.
notes: Telangana's farmer life insurance scheme; premium subsidy differs for loanee vs non-loanee farmers.

description: I am a farmer in Telangana, aged 55.
notes: Telangana's ₹5 lakh farmer insurance cover applies to farmers aged 18-60.

description: I am a farmer, please help me.
notes: State and landholding details are both missing, which are required before any scheme can be suggested.

description: I own 15 acres of farmland in Gujarat and also work as a chartered accountant.
notes: PM-KISAN excludes registered professionals such as chartered accountants who are family members of a farmer household — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I am a farmer's widow in Andhra Pradesh. My husband passed away and the land is now being transferred to me as his legal heir.
notes: Both PM-KISAN and YSR Rythu Bharosa route the benefit to the spouse first, then to the legal heir per land mutation records, on the death of the landholder.

description: I am 65, a farmer in West Bengal with 1.2 acres, and I hold a BPL card.
notes: Age 60+ with BPL status also qualifies for the old-age pension alongside farmer income support.

description: I farm 2 bigha of land in Himachal Pradesh.
notes: Land unit given in 'bigha', which varies by region and isn't directly convertible to acres/hectares without a local conversion — ask for the exact area.

description: I retired as a government schoolteacher and now get a pension of 12,000 rupees a month. I also own 4 acres of ancestral farmland in Karnataka.
notes: PM-KISAN excludes superannuated pensioners whose monthly pension is ₹10,000 or more — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I grow paddy in Karnataka and lost part of my crop in recent floods. I own 4 acres and have valid land papers.
notes: Crop loss with valid land ownership makes PMFBY highly relevant in addition to standard income support.

description: I am a tenant farmer in Andhra Pradesh, but I lease my land from my own brother.
notes: YSR Rythu Bharosa explicitly does not support lease agreements within the same family — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: నేను ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లో గుంటూరు జిల్లాలో రైతును. నాకు 3 ఎకరాల భూమి ఉంది, వరి పండిస్తాను.
notes: Telugu entry: farmer in Guntur district, AP, 3 acres growing paddy.

description: मैं पंजाब में किसान हूँ, मेरे पास 4 एकड़ ज़मीन है। मुझे फसल बीमा के बारे में जानकारी चाहिए।
notes: Hindi entry: farmer in Punjab, 4 acres, asking specifically about crop insurance.

description: I am an SC student in Odisha studying in class 10. Our family income is 1.8 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Class 9-10, SC, income under the ₹2.5 lakh ceiling.

description: I am an ST student in Jharkhand, class 9, family income about 2 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Class 9-10, ST, income under the ₹2.5 lakh ceiling; not already availing another government scholarship.

description: I am an ST student pursuing my undergraduate degree. My family income is 1.9 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Post-matric ST scholarship's income ceiling is ₹2 lakh (not 2.5 lakh) per the scheme's own text — ₹1.9 lakh is under it.

description: I am an ST student in a Master's program. My family income is 2.1 lakh rupees a year.
notes: A deliberate near-miss: post-matric ST scholarship's income ceiling is ₹2 lakh, and 2.1 lakh exceeds it — do not include this scheme.

description: I am a Muslim student in Uttar Pradesh in 5th class. Our family income is 90,000 rupees a year and I scored 65% last year.
notes: Pre-matric minority scholarship: classes 1-10, income ≤₹1 lakh, and at least 50% marks in the previous exam — both met.

description: I am a Christian student in Kerala pursuing my post-matric studies. My family income is 1.8 lakh rupees a year, and I have one older sister who already received this same scholarship two years running.
notes: The post-matric minority scholarship explicitly excludes a student who would be the third sibling in the family to receive it — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I am an OBC student, my family income is 2.3 lakh rupees a year, and I am in my first year of college.
notes: PM-YASASVI post-matric scholarship for OBC/EBC/DNT students: income ≤₹2.5 lakh.

description: I am an OBC student in class 9 studying at a private school. My family income is 2 lakh rupees a year.
notes: PM-YASASVI pre-matric OBC/EBC/DNT scholarship is restricted to students in government schools only — a deliberate exclusion test since this student is in a private school.

description: I am a general category student, not SC, ST or OBC, and my family's income is 95,000 rupees a year. I'm doing my post-matric studies at a government college.
notes: The Dr. Ambedkar EBC post-matric scholarship (for general-category economically backward students) has a ₹1 lakh income ceiling — ₹95,000 qualifies.

description: I am a general category student with a family income of 1.5 lakh rupees a year, doing my post-matric studies.
notes: A deliberate near-miss: the general-category EBC post-matric scholarship's ceiling is ₹1 lakh, and 1.5 lakh exceeds it.

description: I am an OBC student in Bihar, class 8, family income 2.4 lakh rupees, and my attendance last year was around 55%.
notes: The central OBC pre-matric scholarship requires at least 60% attendance in the previous year — 55% falls just short, a deliberate near-miss.

description: I am an SC student in Gujarat who just passed my higher secondary exam and joined a diploma course. Family income is 2.2 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Gujarat's state post-matric SC scholarship: income ≤₹2.5 lakh.

description: I am an OBC student in Uttar Pradesh, class 7, and my parents work in an occupation traditionally considered untouchable. Our income is 1.6 lakh rupees a year.
notes: UP's state OBC pre-matric scholarship specifically covers dependents of traditionally 'untouchable' occupations, income ≤₹2 lakh.

description: I am a student in Nagaland doing my post-matric studies. My family income is 2.3 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Nagaland's state post-matric scholarship: income ≤₹2.5 lakh. Caste category should be confirmed with the applicant, as the scheme record covers a specific category.

description: I need help with my daughter's education.
notes: Very vague — daughter's age/class, state, family income and caste category are all missing. Depending on the answers, this could point to Sukanya Samriddhi (if under 10), a pre/post-matric scholarship, or a state girl-child scheme like Kanyashree.

description: I'm in college and need help paying for my hostel fees.
notes: No caste category, income, or state given — all three are needed before any scholarship can be identified.

description: I am an SC student in Odisha, class 9, and I failed this class last year so I'm repeating it. Family income is 1.5 lakh.
notes: The SC pre-matric scholarship explicitly excludes a second consecutive year of the scholarship for a repeated class — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: నేను ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లో ఎస్టీ కులానికి చెందిన విద్యార్థిని. నేను 10వ తరగతి చదువుతున్నాను, మా కుటుంబ ఆదాయం సంవత్సరానికి రూ. 1,80,000.
notes: Telugu entry: ST student in AP, class 10, income ₹1.8 lakh/year — under the ₹2.5 lakh pre-matric ceiling.

description: मैं उत्तर प्रदेश में रहने वाला ओबीसी छात्र हूँ, कक्षा 9 में पढ़ता हूँ। हमारी पारिवारिक आय सालाना 90,000 रुपये है, और मैं सरकारी स्कूल में पढ़ता हूँ।
notes: Hindi entry: OBC student, UP, class 9, government school, income ₹90,000/year — meets PM-YASASVI pre-matric conditions.

description: I am a 45-year-old widow in Odisha. I hold a BPL ration card.
notes: Meets the 40-79 age range and BPL requirement for the widow pension.

description: I am a 38-year-old widow in Karnataka, BPL family.
notes: Just under the IGNWPS age threshold of 40 — a deliberate near-miss.

description: I was a widow receiving the widow pension, but I remarried last year.
notes: IGNWPS is explicitly discontinued upon remarriage — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: My husband, the only earning member, died last month at age 45. We are a BPL family.
notes: One-time National Family Benefit Scheme payment applies when a breadwinner aged 18-59 in a BPL family dies.

description: I am a widow, please help me.
notes: Age and BPL/income status are both missing, and each changes which pension applies.

description: నేను ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లో 50 ఏళ్ల వితంతువును. నేను దారిద్ర్య రేఖకు దిగువన ఉన్న కుటుంబం నుండి వచ్చాను.
notes: Telugu entry: 50-year-old widow in AP from a BPL family — meets the widow pension's age and poverty criteria.

description: I am 65 years old and live in Tamil Nadu. My family is below the poverty line.
notes: Meets the 60+ and BPL criteria for old-age pension.

description: I am 58 years old and my family holds a BPL card.
notes: Below the 60-year threshold for old-age pension — a deliberate near-miss.

description: I am 85 years old, living in Kerala, and my family is BPL.
notes: Well above the 60-year minimum, and BPL status is confirmed.

description: I am old and need money.
notes: No exact age or BPL/income status given — both are required before recommending anything.

description: मैं राजस्थान में रहने वाली 75 साल की बुज़ुर्ग महिला हूँ। मेरा परिवार गरीबी रेखा से नीचे है।
notes: Hindi entry: 75-year-old BPL woman in Rajasthan — qualifies for the old-age pension.

description: I am 30 years old, with an 85% locomotor disability. My family is BPL.
notes: Meets the 18-79 age range, 80%+ disability, and BPL requirements for the central disability pension.

description: I have a 45% disability, I live in Chandigarh, and my family income is 1.2 lakh rupees a year. I've lived here for 5 years.
notes: Below the 80% central IGNDPS threshold, but meets Chandigarh's own disability pension (40%+ disability, 3+ years' residency, income ≤₹1.5 lakh).

description: I have a 30% disability and live in Chandigarh with a family income of around 1.7 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Below Chandigarh's 40% disability threshold and above its ₹1.5 lakh income ceiling — a deliberate double near-miss.

description: My son is 15 years old and has a 90% disability. We are a BPL family.
notes: IGNDPS requires the beneficiary to be at least 18, so a 15-year-old doesn't yet qualify — flag rather than match.

description: मैं बिहार में रहता हूँ, मेरी उम्र 50 साल है और मुझे 82% विकलांगता है। मेरा परिवार गरीबी रेखा से नीचे है।
notes: Hindi entry: 50 years old, 82% disability, BPL family — meets all IGNDPS criteria.

description: I have a disability, what schemes can I get?
notes: Disability percentage, age, state and income/BPL status are all missing — each affects eligibility.

description: I am a 28-year-old carpenter, this is our family trade, and I've never taken a similar loan before.
notes: Carpentry is one of the 18 PM Vishwakarma trades, no similar loan taken in the past 5 years.

description: I am a blacksmith and I took a Mudra loan two years ago for my workshop.
notes: PM Vishwakarma excludes applicants who availed a similar self-employment loan (PMEGP/PM SVANidhi/Mudra) within the past 5 years — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I work as a government clerk, and I also want to register as a traditional artisan under a craft scheme.
notes: PM Vishwakarma explicitly excludes government employees and their family members.

description: I am a street vendor selling vegetables in Mumbai. I have a Certificate of Vending from the municipal corporation.
notes: Holding a Certificate of Vending from the Urban Local Body is the clearest path to eligibility for PM SVANidhi.

description: I sell vegetables from a cart in a village just outside a town in Karnataka. The town committee gave me a recommendation letter.
notes: PM SVANidhi extends to peri-urban/rural vendors within a Town Vending Committee's geographic limits when they hold a Letter of Recommendation — this vendor qualifies even though outside the town itself.

description: I want to expand my shop, can you help me get a loan?
notes: No loan amount, business type, or location given — needed to decide between Mudra, PMEGP, or PM Vishwakarma.

description: I am unemployed in Odisha, passed 8th standard, and want to set up a manufacturing unit that will cost about 15 lakh rupees.
notes: Meets the minimum education requirement for a manufacturing project above the ₹10 lakh subsidy threshold.

description: I want to start a tailoring business and need a loan of about 3 lakh rupees. I have some tailoring experience and no defaults on any past loans.
notes: Not a family-based traditional trade, and no PMEGP-style manufacturing/service unit named, so a Mudra loan is the closer fit given relevant experience and a clean credit record.

description: I am a fisherman in Kerala and I make and repair fishing nets as our family's traditional work. I'm 30 years old.
notes: Fishing net maker is one of the 18 listed PM Vishwakarma trades.

description: I don't have a bank account. I am an adult and want to open one, and my 11-year-old also wants one.
notes: PMJDY covers both — the child (over 10) can hold an account with guardian support.

description: నేను ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లో 33 ఏళ్ల స్వర్ణకారుడిని (బంగారు నగలు తయారుచేస్తాను). ఇది మా కుటుంబ వృత్తి, మరియు నేను ఇంతకు ముందు ఎలాంటి రుణం తీసుకోలేదు.
notes: Telugu entry: 33-year-old goldsmith in AP, family trade, no prior similar loan — goldsmith is one of the 18 listed trades.

description: I am 22 years old, pregnant with my first child, and I hold a BPL ration card.
notes: First pregnancy with BPL card is a qualifying disadvantaged category, independent of the employment/wage-loss condition.

description: I am pregnant with my first child, I have a job, and I am losing wages because of the pregnancy.
notes: Meets PMMVY's core condition directly: pregnant, employed, and experiencing wage loss due to pregnancy.

description: I am pregnant with twins in my second pregnancy, and the doctor says both will be girls.
notes: Under PMMVY 2.0, the second-child incentive applies specifically to a second pregnancy that results in a multiple birth (twins/triplets) with at least one girl — this case matches exactly.

description: I am pregnant with my second child, a single birth, and the doctor says it's a girl.
notes: A deliberate near-miss: per this scheme's own rule, the 2nd-child girl incentive is tied to a multiple birth (twins/triplets) in the second pregnancy, not a single birth — flag for the model rather than assume eligibility. Source record contradicts itself — eligibility_text says first live birth only; description/benefits give Rs 6,000 for a second girl child (likely PMMVY 2.0 rules mixed with older text). Excluded from metrics.

description: I am pregnant and I work as a permanent employee at a public sector undertaking.
notes: PMMVY excludes women in regular employment with the Central/State Government or a PSU.

description: నేను ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లో ఒక రైతు భార్యను, వయసు 22. ఇది నా మొదటి గర్భం, మరియు నేను ప్రధాన మంత్రి కిసాన్ సమ్మాన్ నిధి లబ్ధిదారురాలిని.
notes: Telugu entry: farmer's wife in AP, 22, first pregnancy, and a PM-KISAN beneficiary — one of PMMVY's listed disadvantaged categories.

description: I just had a baby girl and want to start saving for her future.
notes: Well within the under-10 age limit for opening a Sukanya Samriddhi account.

description: My daughter is 11 years old and I want to open a Sukanya Samriddhi account for her.
notes: SSY accounts can only be opened before the girl turns 10 — a deliberate near-miss.

description: My daughter is 14, unmarried, studying in class 9 at a government school in West Bengal. Our family income is 1 lakh rupees a year.
notes: Kanyashree Prakalpa: girl aged 13-18, unmarried, income ≤₹1.2 lakh, studying classes 8-12 in a government/government-aided school in West Bengal — all met.

description: My daughter is 16 and studies in a private school in West Bengal. Our income is 90,000 rupees a year.
notes: Kanyashree Prakalpa explicitly excludes girls studying in private schools from the annual scholarship — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I want to secure my daughter's future.
notes: Daughter's exact age determines Sukanya Samriddhi eligibility (under 10); state, school type and income determine schemes like Kanyashree.

description: I live in a kutcha house in rural Madhya Pradesh with no shelter of my own, essentially living on alms.
notes: Destitute/houseless households are an automatic-inclusion category under PMAY-Gramin.

description: My family's annual income is 2.5 lakh rupees, we live in a city in Gujarat, and we don't own a pucca house anywhere. It's just my spouse, our unmarried kids, and me.
notes: Falls in the EWS bracket (≤₹3 lakh) for PMAY-Urban; family structure and no-existing-house condition are both met.

description: My family's income is about 8 lakh rupees a year, and I want to know about the home loan interest subsidy in a city.
notes: Falls in the MIG-1 income bracket (₹6-12 lakh) for PMAY-Urban.

description: My family's income is 20 lakh rupees a year, and I want a home loan subsidy under PMAY.
notes: Exceeds the top MIG-2 bracket of ₹18 lakh — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I want a new house under a government scheme, but I already own a house elsewhere and previously received a housing scheme benefit.
notes: PMAY-U explicitly excludes applicants who already own a pucca house anywhere, or who previously availed any housing-related government scheme.

description: I need a house, can you help me?
notes: Rural vs. urban, income, family structure and prior housing benefits are all missing and directly decide eligibility.

description: I am a construction worker in Haryana, registered with the welfare board for two years now. My daughter is getting married.
notes: Haryana's construction workers' welfare board scheme requires at least one year of registered membership — two years comfortably qualifies.

description: I started working as a construction laborer in Haryana three months ago and just registered with the welfare board. My son is getting married next month.
notes: Haryana's scheme requires a minimum of one year of registered membership — three months is a deliberate near-miss.

description: I am a construction worker in Puducherry, registered with the welfare board. My daughter just got admission into a higher education program.
notes: Puducherry's construction workers' welfare board offers higher education finance assistance for a registered worker's child.

description: I do construction work in Haryana but I've never registered with any welfare board.
notes: Welfare board registration is the threshold requirement for these schemes — being unregistered rules this out until the worker registers.

description: I do daily labor work to earn money.
notes: Exact trade, state and welfare board registration status are needed before matching a specific benefit.

description: मैं बिहार में हाथगाड़ी चलाता हूँ, मेरी उम्र 45 साल है। मैं असंगठित क्षेत्र में काम करता हूँ।
notes: Hindi entry: cart puller in Bihar. Occupation and state alone aren't enough here — welfare board registration status would need to be confirmed for any Bihar-specific unorganized-worker scheme.

description: I heard about something called 'Universal Farmer Bonus Yojana', can I apply for it?
notes: This scheme name does not correspond to any real scheme — the system should not invent or guess a matching scheme.

description: I earn about 15 lakh rupees a year in my job, what government schemes am I eligible for?
notes: Most schemes in this catalog are means-tested for low-income or vulnerable households; a high-income salaried profile doesn't match any of them as described.

description: I already have an LPG gas connection at home, but I heard about a free gas connection scheme. Can I get another one?
notes: PMUY explicitly requires the household not already have an LPG connection — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I am a woman from a poor household in Bihar and I don't have an LPG connection at home.
notes: Adult woman from a poor household with no existing LPG connection meets PMUY's core condition.

description: I am 25, unmarried, and want to open a small savings scheme for myself.
notes: Sukanya Samriddhi is only for a girl child under 10 opened by a guardian — this applicant is an adult opening an account for themself, so it doesn't apply; ask what kind of savings goal they have in mind.

description: I am a farmer's family in Maharashtra. One of our sons works as a government clerk and pays income tax, but the rest of us just farm the land.
notes: Both PM-KISAN and Namo Shetkari treat the whole farmer family as one unit — if any member is a government employee or income-tax payer, the entire family is excluded, not just that member.

description: I want a Vishwakarma loan, but I am the only earning member and I'm also the sole registered farmer in the family already getting PM-KISAN.
notes: Receiving PM-KISAN doesn't disqualify PM Vishwakarma by itself, but the applicant needs to actually be engaged in one of the 18 listed artisan trades — that hasn't been stated, so don't add pmv without confirming the trade.

description: I am a 24-year-old wanting to join the Atal Pension Yojana. I have a savings bank account and I don't pay income tax.
notes: Age 24 is within the 18-40 joining window, and the applicant isn't an income-tax payer.

description: I am 42 years old and want to join the Atal Pension Yojana.
notes: A deliberate near-miss: the APY joining window closes at 40 years.

description: I am a farmer in Andhra Pradesh who converted part of my farmland into a house plot last year, but it's still shown as farmland in the revenue records.
notes: YSR Rythu Bharosa explicitly excludes land converted to house sites or other non-agricultural use, whether or not the revenue records have been updated yet — a deliberate exclusion test.

description: I am a weaver in Odisha, this is our traditional family craft, and I'm 40 years old.
notes: Handloom weaving as a standalone craft doesn't clearly match any of PM Vishwakarma's 18 named trades — ask for the exact craft/tools used before matching, rather than assuming it fits.

description: I am a farmer's widow in Andhra Pradesh, 44 years old, and my late husband cultivated 1.5 acres of leased land as a tenant. He passed away three months ago.
notes: As a landless tenant cultivator's family, YSR Rythu Bharosa's tenant-farmer provision is the relevant path (not PM-KISAN, which needs ownership); confirm she is now the recognized cultivator on the lease.
